prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” company for everyone — the right roofer depends on your exact location, roof type (asphalt shingle, metal, tile, etc.), budget and how soon you need the work. If you want, give me your Miami zip code and the roof material you prefer and I’ll pull a short, customized shortlist with recent ratings and contact info.

In the meantime, here’s how to find and pick the best hurricane‑rated roof contractor in Miami and what to require:

What to require / check
- Valid license and insurance: verify the contractor’s Florida/DBPR roofing license and ask for current general liability and workers’ comp certificates.  
- Miami‑Dade product approvals: materials and assembly must meet Miami‑Dade County (HVHZ) requirements — ask for Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) numbers for the products and for proof the installation will follow the NOA/installation instructions.  
- Manufacturer certifications: look for GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, or manufacturer certification for metal/tile. Certified installers get better warranties.  
- Fortified/IBHS options: ask whether they can install to IBHS Fortified Roof standards (if you want the higher resilience and insurance benefits).  
- Permits & inspections: contractor should pull permits and coordinate municipal inspections.  
- Written estimate & scope: get a detailed written contract listing materials, fastening schedules, underlayment, ventilation, flashing, removal/disposal, start/completion dates, clean‑up and payment schedule.  
- Warranties: get both manufacturer warranty and contractor workmanship warranty in writing; ask if warranties are transferable.  
- References & portfolio: ask for recent hurricane‑rated project references in Miami and photos; call them.  
- Price checks: obtain at least 3 bids for comparison.

Technical items to confirm (important for hurricane performance)
- Secondary water barrier or self‑adhering underlayment at eaves and rakes.  
- Correct fasteners (ring‑shank nails or screws) and spacing per NOA/manufacturer.  
- Proper tile anchoring or mechanical fastening for tiles.  
- Secure rakes, eaves, soffits, fascia and hip/ridge details.  
- Uplift‑rated vents and sealed roof penetrations.  
- Tie‑downs/straps for roof-to-wall connections if structural work is needed.

Questions to ask a contractor
- “Are you licensed in Florida? What is your license number?”  
- “Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can you provide certificates?”  
- “Can you provide the Miami‑Dade NOA numbers for the products and the installation instructions?”  
- “Are you a certified installer for the manufacturer? Can I see the certification?”  
- “Will you pull permits and handle inspections?”  
- “What warranties do you provide, and are they transferable?”  
- “Can you give references for recent hurricane‑rated jobs in my area?”

Red flags
- No license or insurance.  
- Refuses written contract or demands large cash up front.  
- Vague answers about Miami‑Dade approvals and installation details.  
- Poor/no online reviews or unresolved BBB complaints.  
- Unmarked vehicle or no local address.

If you want, tell me:
- Your Miami zip code, roof material (shingle/metal/tile), and whether you want Fortified or maximum wind rating. I’ll prepare a short list of top-rated, hurricane‑experienced roofers near you with notes on credentials and recent reviews.
